Quick security readout after reviewing Acme's redline and our telemetry surface: 

- What we currently surface: runtime logs contain timestamps, model_id (internal identifier), request metadata (client ID, region) and basic diagnostics. We do not persist raw request payloads in telemetry; any stored traces used for debugging are redacted and access-controlled.
- Subprocessor access: our analytics/observability vendor can access aggregated telemetry and traces under strict access control and MFA. They do not have key material or raw customer payloads.

Implications and suggested contract language:
- We can accept a reasonable prior-notice requirement for subprocessors that gain access to runtime logs. Recommended wording: 
  "Provider will provide Customer with written notice at least thirty (30) days prior to onboarding any subprocessor that will have access to runtime logs, model interaction metadata, or unredacted debugging traces."
- On routing: there are two classes of routing change — transient automated fallbacks (per-request, milliseconds) and persistent routing changes (e.g., moving a tenant to a regional variant or permanently swapping to a fallback model family). We should be explicit: transient fallbacks are operational resiliency and cannot always be pre-notified; persistent changes should include advance notice. Suggested wording: 
  "Provider will provide notice prior to any permanent change in routing that materially affects data residency or model family used for Customer requests; transient per-request fallbacks for operational resiliency are excluded. Provider will also publish a post-change summary describing the scope and duration of such changes."

Controls we can offer: allowlist for subprocessors for enterprise customers, 30-day notice, redact/pseudonymize model identifiers in telemetry, audit trail linking subprocessor access to app-level ops.

I'll attach a short security impact summary. If legal needs stronger guarantees we should loop in procurement + legal to discuss carveouts (e.g., emergency remediation).

Olga

Hi Maria / Acme team — thanks for the redlines and patience while we reviewed internally. Below is our consolidated position and a proposed redline you can review quickly. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you prefer.

Summary of position (operational + contract):
- Subprocessor notice: we can commit to written notice at least thirty (30) days prior to onboarding any subprocessor that will have access to runtime logs, model interaction metadata, or unredacted debugging traces. We will provide the subprocessor name, site of processing, and a summary of the data types to be accessed.

- Routing / fallback notice: we distinguish between (A) transient per-request fallbacks (automated, milliseconds, used to maintain latency/availability) and (B) persistent or planned routing changes that materially affect data residency or change the model family used for Customer requests. We cannot guarantee pre-notification for transient per-request fallbacks. For persistent changes (e.g., tenant migration to a regional deployment or permanent model swap) we will provide written notice prior to the effective date and publish a post-change summary.

Proposed contract text (suggested):
"Provider will provide Customer with written notice at least thirty (30) days prior to onboarding any subprocessor that will have access to runtime logs, model interaction metadata, or unredacted debugging traces. Provider will provide the subprocessor's name, processing location, and a short description of the data types the subprocessor will process.

Provider will provide Customer with prior written notice for any permanent change in routing that materially affects data residency or the model family used for Customer requests. Transient, automated per-request fallbacks performed to maintain service availability are excluded from this notice requirement. Provider will publish a post-change summary describing the scope and duration of such permanent routing changes."

Next steps: if this wording is acceptable, we can incorporate it into the DPA and circulate a redline (attached: proposed_dpa_redline.docx) for countersignature. If Acme needs a shorter notice window or additional guarantees, please propose alternative language and we will escalate to legal/security.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
